Charles-McClintock Wilson | Nurphoto | Getty Images Microsoft on Thursday announced plans to raise $25 billion in bonds, taking advantage of its healthy credit rating to support its infrastructure expansion. The software maker holds a top-tier AAA rating with S&P, a credit agency. Management is targeting $170 billion in 2026 capital expenditures, as the company looks to meet heavy demand from artificial intelligence labs Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as other clients. "Microsoft intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes, which may include, among other things, funding for working capital, capital expenditures, repurchases of capital stock, acquisitions, and repayment of existing debt," according to a statement . The offerings should close on Nov. 4, the company said. Amazon and Alphabet have engaged the bond market to support infrastructure projects this year, and AI-focused cloud CoreWeave has also relied on the debt market to broaden its data center footprint. Investors have turned more skittish on companies with tall debt piles as central bankers raise interest rates to fight inflation. Microsoft will access additional funding sources to complement its own cash flow generation when conditions are attractive, Amy Hood, its finance chief, said on the company's earnings call on Wednesday. "There's a form of financing called leasing, and we've been using that one as a vehicle," she said. "We're fortunate to have access in the debt markets, given where our ratings are, and we haven't yet tapped that." Microsoft reported positive free cash flow on Wednesday, differentiating itself from Alphabet, whose cash flow was negative for the second quarter in a row. Last week Meta said it had negative free cash flow, and on Thursday Amazon reported negative free cash flow. Also on Wednesday, Oracle unveiled plans to raise $10 billion in new debt and said it anticipates a return to positive free cash flow in the second half of its 2028 fiscal year. headlines.article_text: Friday's big stock stories: What’s likely to move the market Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Stocks @ Night is a daily newsletter delivered after hours, giving you a first look at tomorrow and last look at today. Sign up for free to receive it directly in your inbox. Here's what CNBC TV's producers were watching as Alphabet shares dropped 12%, and what's on the radar for the next session. Big Oil ExxonMobil reports on " Squawk Box ." The stock is up almost 17% in three months and hit a new high on Tuesday. CEO Darren Woods will be on the big show live with Becky Quick, Andrew Ross Sorkin and Joe Kernen in the 8 a.m. hour ET. Chevron reports as well. The stock is up about 21% in three months. It hit a high Monday. CEO Mike Wirth will be on " Squawk on the Street " in the 9 a.m. hour Friday. West Texas Intermediate crude futures are up about 22% in three months, while Brent is up about 27%. XOM 3M mountain ExxonMobil in the past three months Amazon The web giant missed earnings estimates in the third quarter. In her Thursday night article, CNBC's Annie Palmer reports CEO Andy Jassy said the company will "spend meaningfully more in 2027," but has a "clear line of sight to attractive financial returns." Jim Cramer covered the earnings on "Mad Money." He said, "I do think the call was stronger than the report" and "the web services business is extraordinary." But Cramer also said, "This market is not in the mood for longer-term scenarios." Cramer is waiting though before buying. He said, "When the smoke clears… buy, buy buy." Amazon shares are down almost 7% after hours. The stock is now off 16% from the high. We'll be watching it closely Friday on " Morning Call, " starting at 5 a.m. Starbucks The company beat on earnings but missed on revenue. CEO Brian Niccol said in a video release, "We enter fiscal 2027 with momentum, a clear set of priorities and higher ambitions for what Starbucks can become." CNBC's Amelia Lucas is following the company's earnings report. She wrote in her Thursday night article : "Starbucks is projecting North American same-store sales growth of 4% for the fiscal year." The stock is down about 2% after hours. Shares are up 12% in October and off 4.5% from the August high. At 9 a.m. Friday, Niccol will be on " Squawk on the Street " with Jim Cramer, Carl Quintanilla and David Faber. SBUX 1M mountain Starbucks in the past month AstraZeneca reports Hopefully you'll be asleep when the numbers cross at 2:30 a.m. ET. That's 11:30 p.m. if you're on the West Coast. AstraZeneca is little changed in three months, but shares are down 5.8% in six months. The stock is off 18% from the February high. Apple CNBC's MacKenzie Sigalos will report ahead of Apple CEO John Ternus' first earnings release on Monday. The stock hit a new high last week. Shares are up 28% in 2026.
